ai_show_review.summary: High‑octane MIT set with blistering Dancin' and soaring Morning Dew
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert bursts with angry, high‑energy playing fueled by the recent Kent State tragedy and cold weather. Standout performances include a ferocious Dancin' In The Street, a monster Good Lovin'/Saint Stephen/Not Fade Away sequence and a soaring Morning Dew. Jerry’s guitar is on fire while Phil delivers devastating bass runs.
ai_show_review.review: On May 6, 1970 the Grateful Dead took over Kresge Plaza at MIT with a set that still feels like a lightning‑strike of raw intensity. From the opening Dancin' In The Street the band rode a wave of anger and cold‑weather urgency, Jerry thrashing his SG with a metallic twang while Phil unleashed one of his most devastating bass runs. Pigpen’s organ swelled on Good Lovin', adding soulful depth despite an early mic glitch, and the ensuing jam into Saint Stephen and Not Fade Away flows like a seamless improvisational peak. The second half never lets up – China Cat Sunflower segues straight into I Know You Rider before launching into a tight, vocal‑driven Next Time You See Me and the hauntingly beautiful Morning Dew, where Jerry’s solo is described as a “self‑generating source of electricity.” Bill Kreutzmann anchors the set with powerful, atmospheric drumming that even warmed the chilly audience, while Mickey Hart adds his usual percussive texture. Overall, the show captures the band at a feverish high point, delivering relentless energy and several monster moments that make this MIT gig a must‑listen.

best_recording.reason: Sharp mono soundboard feed that captures the full intensity of the performance with clear, crisp detail despite occasional glitches; widely regarded as the most complete and listenable version.

key_highlights: Incendiary Dancin' In The Street channels the era’s anger and raw power
Monster Good Lovin'/Saint Stephen/Not Fade Away seamless jam sequence
Soaring Morning Dew featuring Jerry’s electrifying solo
Pigpen’s soulful organ on Good Lovin' adds depth to the set

band_performance.Jerry: Ferocious, metallic‑twang guitar work; described as a self‑generating source of electricity with powerful solos on Morning Dew and tearing through Dancin' In The Street.
band_performance.Phil: Devastating bass runs, especially on Dancing in the Streets; lead‑bass quality shines on Good Lovin' and Morning Dew, providing telepathic interplay with Jerry.
band_performance.Bob: Urgent vocals that drive the set, leads on Not Fade Away and shares a vocal duel with Pigpen on Good Lovin'; solid rhythm guitar throughout.
band_performance.Pigpen: Vital organ and vocal contributions, especially on Good Lovin' where his soulful texture adds depth despite an early mic glitch.
band_performance.Billy: Powerful, atmospheric drumming that underpins the jams; strong drum intro on Good Lovin' and steady groove that warmed hands during the chilly show.
